title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Features
abstract: Adversarial examples have attracted significant attention in machine learning, but the reasons for their existence and pervasiveness remain unclear. We demonstrate that adversarial examples can be directly attributed to the presence of non-robust features: features derived from patterns in the data distribution that are highly predictive, yet brittle and incomprehensible to humans. After capturing these features within a theoretical framework, we establish their widespread existence in standard datasets. Finally, we present a simple setting where we can rigorously tie the phenomena we observe in practice to a misalignment between the (human-specified) notion of robustness and the inherent geometry of the data.
research_question: Why do adversarial examples exist and are pervasive? The paper investigates whether adversarial examples can be attributed to non-robust features in the data.
core_contribution: Adversarial examples are shown to arise from non-robust features: predictive but brittle features in the data. The paper demonstrates that these features exist in standard datasets and that models' reliance on them leads to adversarial vulnerability.
conclusion: Adversarial examples are not bugs but features inherent to the data distribution. Achieving robustness requires explicitly discouraging models from using non-robust features.
key_findings: Non-robust features exist in standard datasets and are highly predictive for classification.
Removing non-robust features from a dataset allows training a robust classifier with standard training.
Training on a dataset consisting only of non-robust features (with seemingly incorrect labels) yields good standard accuracy, showing non-robust features suffice for generalization.
Adversarial transferability occurs because different models learn similar non-robust features.
Theoretically, adversarial vulnerability can be tied to a misalignment between the human-specified robustness metric and the inherent data geometry.
limitation: The findings do not preclude adversarial vulnerability arising from other phenomena besides non-robust features.
The theoretical framework does not fully capture the finer-grained phenomena observed in experiments.
future_direction: Bridging the gap between the theoretical framework and the experimental findings.
Developing methods to effectively discourage the use of non-robust features during training.
